title: Unpredictable what actually will be pasted due to copy-only-selection item not being visually differentiated in any way
line: The clipboard popup now marks which entry Ctrl+V pastes and which one middle-click pastes.
explanation: With 'Text selected with the pointer' saved in history and not kept in sync with the clipboard, the clipboard and the selection hold different entries, but Klipper only knew the history order, so the popup showed every entry the same way and the top one was often the selection, not what Ctrl+V pastes. The change (Tomáš Hnyk's draft MR !6887, rebased on master) makes the history model remember which entry each buffer holds and exposes it as two roles plus a tracksBothBuffers property; when the buffers are tracked separately every row reserves a two-icon column at its leading edge, with a paste icon on the clipboard entry and a mouse icon on the selection entry, so all entries stay aligned.

commits.message:
klipper: Mark which entry is in the clipboard and which in the selection

With the selection saved in history and not synced, nothing showed which
entry Ctrl+V and which middle-click would paste. Klipper now tracks both
buffers and the popup marks each with an icon and a tooltip.

BUG: 355841

media.caption: Master: clipboard 'first', selection 'second' then 'third': all three rows look alike and nothing says what Ctrl+V or middle-click pastes
Same steps: 'third' has the mouse icon (middle-click), 'first' the paste icon (Ctrl+V), 'second' none, and all three texts line up
After picking 'second' from the popup it is in both buffers and gets both icons; the other rows keep the same indent
